questions.question: Who has been honoured with the Goldman Environmental Prize 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alok Shukla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alok Shukla is an environmental activist from India known for his extensive work in forest conservation.
 
• He has been recognized for his efforts in protecting the rights of indigenous communities and their natural habitats.
 
• Alok Shukla's initiatives have led to significant policy changes and increased awareness about environmental issues in India.
 
• The Goldman Environmental Prize, often referred to as the "Green Nobel," honors grassroots environmental heroes from the world’s six inhabited continental regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goldman Environmental Prize:**

 
 
• Established in 1989 by philanthropists Richard and Rhoda Goldman.
 
• Aims to recognize individuals for sustained and significant efforts to protect and enhance the natural environment, often at great personal risk.
 
• The prize includes a significant monetary award and international recognition.
 
 
 
• **Forest Conservation:**
 
 
• Involves the practice of planning and maintaining forested areas for the benefit and sustainability of future generations.
 
• Critical for maintaining biodiversity, regulating climate, and ensuring the livelihoods of indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Rights:**
 
 
• Refers to the recognition and protection of the rights of indigenous peoples, including their land, culture, and way of life.
 
• Integral to the conservation of biodiversity as indigenous communities often play a crucial role in maintaining their natural environments.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Policy Changes:**
 
 
• Involves the amendment of laws and regulations to better protect the environment and promote sustainable practices.
 
• Can result from grassroots activism, scientific research, and public advocacy.

questions.question: In which year and city/cities India hosted the FIH Men’s World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023 Bhubaneswar and Rourkela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India hosted the FIH Men's World Cup in **2023**.
 
• The event was held in **Bhubaneswar and Rourkela**, cities located in the state of Odisha.
 
• The tournament took place from **January 13 to January 29, 2023**.
 
• This was the fourth time India hosted the FIH Men's World Cup, with previous editions in 1982, 2010, and 2018.
 
• The Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar and the newly constructed Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium in Rourkela were the two venues for the matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIH Men's World Cup**

 
 
• Organized by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), the Men's Hockey World Cup is a prestigious field hockey competition.
 
• The tournament is held every four years, featuring the best national teams from around the world.
 
• The first edition of the Men's Hockey World Cup was held in 1971 in Barcelona, Spain.
 
• Pakistan has been the most successful team in the history of the tournament, winning it four times.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga Stadium**
 
 
• Located in Bhubaneswar, the Kalinga Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium primarily used for field hockey.
 
• It has hosted several international hockey tournaments, including the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup.
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of around 15,000 spectators.
 
 
 
• **Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium**
 
 
• Situated in Rourkela, Odisha, this is a newly constructed stadium for the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup.
 
• It is named after the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda.
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of approximately 20,000, making it one of the largest hockey stadiums in India.
 
 
 
• **India's Hockey History**
 
 
• India has a rich history in field hockey, having won eight Olympic gold medals.
 
• The Indian men's hockey team is one of the most successful teams in the sport's history.
 
• India won the Hockey World Cup in 1975, held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

 D.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Karewas** are lacustrine deposits found in the **Kashmir region** (A-II).
 
• **Barchans** are crescent-shaped sand dunes found predominantly in the **Thar desert** (B-IV).
 
• **Mahendragiri** is a peak located in the **Eastern Ghats** (C-I).
 
• The **Northern Circar** refers to the coastal plain along the **Bay of Bengal** (D-III).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karewas**:

 
 
• Karewas are thick deposits of glacial clay and other materials, including boulders, found in the valleys of the Kashmir region.
 
• These deposits are important for the cultivation of saffron, a significant cash crop in Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Barchans**:
 
 
• Barchans are formed by wind action in arid regions and are characterized by their crescent shape with horns pointing downwind.
 
• They indicate the direction of prevailing winds and are prominent features of desert landscapes.
 
 
 
• **Mahendragiri**:
 
 
• Mahendragiri is the second-highest peak in the Eastern Ghats, located in the Gajapati district of Odisha.
 
• The peak is associated with various legends from the Mahabharata, adding cultural significance to the region.
 
 
 
• **Northern Circar**:
 
 
• The Northern Circars is a historical term for the coastal region along the Bay of Bengal, stretching from Andhra Pradesh to Odisha.
 
• This region was significant during the colonial era for its strategic and economic importance.

questions.question: By which of the following Acts did the rule of the East India Company end in India, and the rule of the crown begin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act of 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act of 1858 was enacted by the British Parliament in the wake of the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• This Act marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and the beginning of direct rule by the British Crown.
 
• The Act provided for the liquidation of the East India Company and the transfer of its functions to the British Crown.
 
• It established the office of the Secretary of State for India and the Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• This was the first attempt to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India and establish a system of control over its administration.
 
• It provided for the appointment of a Governor-General of Bengal and four councillors to assist him.
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:**
 
 
• Also known as the East India Company Act, this Act was introduced by the British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.
 
• It provided for the establishment of a Board of Control to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the Company in India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**
 
 
• This Act ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• It allowed missionaries to come to India to spread Christianity and permitted local subjects to receive education.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act of 1853:**
 
 
• This Act was the last of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament.
 
• It introduced an open competition system for the selection of civil servants and separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.

questions.question: Which state of India is at bottom according to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) India Index, published by NITI Aayog in July 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar ranks at the bottom of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) India Index published by NITI Aayog in July 2024.
 
• The SDG India Index evaluates the progress of states and union territories in achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals.
 
• Bihar has consistently been among the lower-ranked states in previous editions of the SDG India Index.
 
• The state's performance is particularly low in areas such as poverty alleviation, quality education, and infrastructure development.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to improve the state's performance through various developmental programs and policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**

 
 
• The SDGs are a set of 17 global goals established by the United Nations to address various social, economic, and environmental challenges.
 
• They were adopted in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
 
• The goals cover areas such as poverty, education, health, gender equality, clean water, and climate action.
 
• Each goal has specific targets and indicators to measure progress.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) is the premier policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• It was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• NITI Aayog aims to foster cooperative federalism and promote sustainable development in India.
 
• It plays a critical role in formulating strategic and long-term policies for the country's development.
 
 
 
• **India's SDG Index**
 
 
• The SDG India Index is an annual report published by NITI Aayog to track the progress of Indian states and union territories towards achieving the SDGs.
 
• It uses a range of indicators to assess performance in various areas such as health, education, gender equality, and economic growth.
 
• The index helps identify areas requiring policy intervention and resource allocation.
 
• It encourages competition among states to improve their rankings and overall development.
 
 
 
• **Developmental Challenges in Bihar**
 
 
• Bihar faces several developmental challenges, including high poverty rates, inadequate infrastructure, and low literacy levels.
 
• The state government has initiated various programs to address these issues, such as improving access to quality education and healthcare.
 
• Efforts are also being made to enhance agricultural productivity and create employment opportunities.
 
• Despite these initiatives, significant progress is still needed to achieve the SDGs in Bihar.

questions.question: From where was the concept of directive principles borrowed in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Irish Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
 
• The Irish Constitution itself was inspired by the Spanish Constitution.
 
• Directive Principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy.
 
• These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• They are included in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**:

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• They are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by the courts.
 
• These rights provide civil liberties to all citizens and protect individuals from any arbitrary actions of the state.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**:
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution, under Article 51A.
 
• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, inspired by the Constitution of the USSR.
 
• They serve as a reminder to citizens that they must also fulfill their responsibilities towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **Preamble**:
 
 
• The Preamble to the Indian Constitution outlines the objectives of the Constitution.
 
• It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
 
• The Preamble was inspired by the American Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers**:
 
 
• The principle of separation of powers divides the government into three branches: the Legislature, the Executive, and the Judiciary.
 
• This ensures a system of checks and balances, preventing any one branch from gaining too much power.
 
• The doctrine of separation of powers is fundamental to the functioning of a democracy.

questions.question: In the interim budget of the union government, what budget has been allocated for Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan for the Financial Year 2024-25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹37,500 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The allocation for Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan in the interim budget for the Financial Year 2024-25 is ₹37,500 crore.
 
• Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan is an overarching program for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12.
 
• This initiative aims at improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities for schooling and equitable learning outcomes.
 
• The budget allocation is intended to support initiatives such as digital education, infrastructure development, and teacher training programs.
 
• It emphasizes inclusive and equitable quality education and promotes lifelong learning opportunities for all as per the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan**

 
 
• This scheme was launched in 2018 by merging three erstwhile schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE).
 
• It aims to support states in the implementation of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.
 
• The program emphasizes the quality of education and aims to bridge gender and social category gaps in school education.
 
• It includes provisions for the development of school infrastructure, such as building classrooms, laboratories, libraries, and providing basic amenities like toilets and drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009, mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years in India.
 
• It emphasizes the need to eliminate barriers to educational access, retention, and quality.
 
• The act prescribes norms and standards for schools, including pupil-teacher ratios, infrastructure, and teacher qualifications.
 
• It also includes provisions for ensuring children's right to be taught in an inclusive environment.
 
 
 
• **Digital Education Initiatives**
 
 
• Digital education initiatives under Samagra Shiksha aim to leverage technology to improve the quality of education.
 
• These initiatives include the introduction of smart classrooms, e-learning content, and digital literacy programs for students and teachers.
 
• The DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) platform is a key component, providing resources for teachers and students.
 
• The initiatives aim to bridge the digital divide and ensure equitable access to quality education for all students.
 
 
 
• **Teacher Training and Development**
 
 
• The scheme includes provisions for continuous professional development and training of teachers to enhance their skills and competencies.
 
• Training programs focus on pedagogical techniques, subject knowledge, use of technology in classrooms, and inclusive education practices.
 
• Capacity building of school leaders and administrators is also a key component to ensure effective school management.
 
• Regular assessments and evaluations are conducted to measure the impact of training programs on teaching-learning processes.

questions.question: What is the name of the astronaut who was selected for the Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station (ISS) in August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shubhanshu Shukla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shubhanshu Shukla has been selected for the Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station (ISS) in August 2024.
 
• The Axiom-4 mission is part of a series of missions organized by Axiom Space to facilitate private and commercial spaceflight.
 
• Shubhanshu Shukla will be among the few astronauts representing India in international space missions, marking a significant achievement for the country.
 
• The mission aims to conduct various scientific experiments and technology demonstrations on the ISS.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Axiom Space**

 
 
• Axiom Space is a private space company focused on building the world’s first commercial space station.
 
• The company collaborates with NASA and other space agencies to facilitate commercial missions to the ISS.
 
 
 
• **International Space Station (ISS)**
 
 
• The ISS is a multinational collaborative project involving space agencies like NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, and CSA.
 
• It serves as a microgravity and space environment research laboratory where scientific research is conducted in astrobiology, astronomy, meteorology, physics, and other fields.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Spaceflight**
 
 
• Commercial spaceflight refers to space travel conducted by private companies rather than government agencies.
 
• This sector is growing rapidly with companies like SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Axiom Space leading the way.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Experiments on ISS**
 
 
• Experiments conducted on the ISS cover a wide range of fields including biology, human research, physics, and materials science.
 
• These experiments take advantage of the unique microgravity environment to achieve results not possible on Earth.

questions.question: In which year was Pitt’s India Act passed by the British Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pitt's India Act, also known as the East India Company Act of 1784, was passed by the British Parliament in 1784.
 
• The Act was named after the then British Prime Minister, William Pitt the Younger.
 
• It was introduced to correct the deficiencies of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• The Act established a dual system of control over British India, between the British Government and the East India Company.
 
• A Board of Control was created to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773**

 
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It recognized the political and administrative functions of the Company and laid the foundation for a central administration in India.
 
• The Act established the position of Governor-General of Bengal and a council of four members to assist him.
 
 
 
• **Dual System of Control**
 
 
• The Pitt's India Act introduced a dual system of governance, where the control of political affairs was divided between the British Government and the East India Company.
 
• The Board of Control, representing the British Government, had the ultimate authority over the Company's civil, military, and revenue activities in India.
 
 
 
• **Board of Control**
 
 
• The Board of Control consisted of six members, including the Secretary of State for India.
 
• It had the power to supervise and direct all operations of the East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Act**
 
 
• Pitt's India Act laid the foundation for British control over Indian administration and marked the beginning of the British Government's direct involvement in Indian affairs.
 
• It significantly curtailed the autonomy of the East India Company and increased the accountability of its officials.

questions.question: Who inaugurated India’s first off-grid Green Hydrogen Plant in the Stainless Steel Sector at Hisar in March 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiraditya M Scindia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotiraditya M Scindia, the Union Minister of Steel, inaugurated India's first off-grid Green Hydrogen Plant in the Stainless Steel Sector at Hisar in March 2024.
 
• This initiative aligns with India's commitment to reducing carbon emissions and transitioning towards renewable energy sources.
 
• The Green Hydrogen Plant is set to produce hydrogen using renewable energy, marking a significant step in the stainless steel sector's sustainability efforts.
 
• Hisar, located in Haryana, has been chosen as the site for this pioneering project due to its strategic importance in the steel industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Hydrogen**

 
 
• Green Hydrogen is produced using renewable energy sources, such as wind or solar power, through the process of electrolysis.
 
• It is considered a clean fuel, emitting only water vapor and air, making it an environmentally friendly alternative to fossil fuels.
 
• Green Hydrogen plays a crucial role in achieving zero-carbon targets and is pivotal for sectors like transportation, industry, and energy.
 
 
 
• **Stainless Steel Sector**
 
 
• The stainless steel sector is vital for various industries, including construction, automotive, and manufacturing, due to its corrosion-resistant properties.
 
• Incorporating green hydrogen in stainless steel production can significantly reduce the industry's carbon footprint.
 
 
 
• **Electrolysis**
 
 
• Electrolysis is the process of using electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.
 
• This process is crucial for producing green hydrogen, which relies on renewable energy to be sustainable.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Sources**
 
 
• Renewable energy sources include wind, solar, hydro, and geothermal energy.
 
• These sources are sustainable and have a significantly lower environmental impact compared to fossil fuels.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the state shall take steps, to secure the participation of workers in the management of industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 43A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 43A** of the Indian Constitution was incorporated by the **42nd Amendment** in 1976.
 
• This article directs the State to take steps to **secure the participation of workers** in the management of industries.
 
• It aims to promote **industrial democracy** and strengthen **worker involvement** in decision-making processes.
 
• The provision is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, which guide the State in formulating and implementing policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**:

 
 
• The DPSP are guidelines/principles given to the federal institutes governing the State of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are contained in Part IV of the Constitution, spanning Articles 36-51.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**:
 
 
• This amendment, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought about comprehensive changes to the Constitution.
 
• It added new provisions related to the duties of citizens, the judiciary, and the functioning of the State.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Democracy**:
 
 
• It refers to the involvement of workers in the decision-making processes of a company or industry.
 
• The aim is to ensure that workers have a voice in the decisions that affect their work and lives.
 
 
 
• **Workers’ Participation in Management**:
 
 
• This concept involves employees being part of the management processes of their organization.
 
• It can take various forms, including joint consultation, works councils, and board representation.

questions.question: In August 2024, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Panacea Biotec announced the initiation of the first-ever Phase 3 clinical trial for which of the following vaccines in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dengue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In August 2024, the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Panacea Biotec announced the initiation of the first-ever Phase 3 clinical trial for a Dengue vaccine in India.
 
• The trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the tetravalent Dengue vaccine developed by Panacea Biotec.
 
• This vaccine targets all four serotypes of the Dengue virus, which is crucial for providing comprehensive protection.
 
• The Phase 3 trial will involve thousands of participants across multiple sites in India to ensure robust data.
 
• The goal is to develop a vaccine that can significantly reduce the incidence of Dengue, a mosquito-borne viral infection that poses a significant public health challenge in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dengue Virus**

 
 
• Dengue is caused by four distinct serotypes of the Dengue virus (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4).
 
• Infection with one serotype provides lifelong immunity against that serotype but not against the others.
 
• Subsequent infections with different serotypes increase the risk of severe Dengue, also known as Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF).
 
 
 
• **Clinical Trials**
 
 
• Clinical trials are research studies performed in people to evaluate a medical, surgical, or behavioral intervention.
 
• They are the primary way researchers find out if a new treatment, like a new drug or diet or medical device, is safe and effective in people.
 
• Phase 3 trials are conducted to confirm and expand on the safety and effectiveness results obtained in Phase 1 and 2 trials.
 
 
 
• **ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research)**
 
 
• ICMR is the apex body in India for the formulation, coordination, and promotion of biomedical research.
 
• It is one of the oldest and largest medical research bodies in the world.
 
• ICMR plays a crucial role in the development and implementation of health policies in India.
 
 
 
• **Panacea Biotec**
 
 
• Panacea Biotec is one of India's leading biotechnology companies.
 
• The company focuses on research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of pharmaceuticals, vaccines, and biosimilars.
 
• Panacea Biotec has a strong portfolio of vaccines and has contributed significantly to public health initiatives in India.

questions.question: The estimated rate of unemployment for the year 2018–19 in urban areas was _______%.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) 7.7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The estimated rate of unemployment for the year 2018-19 in urban areas was 7.7%, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).
 
• This survey was conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The unemployment rate indicates the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking employment.
 
• The survey provides key indicators of the labor market, including employment status and labor force participation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**:

 
 
• The PLFS was launched by the National Statistical Office (NSO) in April 2017.
 
• It aims to provide quarterly estimates of key labor market indicators in urban areas and annual estimates in both urban and rural areas.
 
• The survey covers indicators like the employment status, unemployment rate, labor force participation rate, and worker population ratio.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate**:
 
 
• The unemployment rate is the percentage of the total labor force that is unemployed but actively seeking employment and willing to work.
 
• It is a key indicator of the labor market's health and overall economic performance.
 
 
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO)**:
 
 
• The NSO operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• It is responsible for conducting large-scale surveys and providing key statistical data for the country.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**:
 
 
• The LFPR is the percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• It is an important measure of the active portion of an economy's labor force.

questions.question: In which of the following countries does the industrial sector contribute less towards the GDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pakistan's industrial sector contributes significantly less to the GDP compared to other major economies like India, China, and Japan.
 
• As of the latest data, the industrial sector in Pakistan contributes around 20% to its GDP.
 
• In contrast, the industrial sector in China and India contributes approximately 30% and 25% to their respective GDPs.
 
• Japan, being a highly industrialized nation, has its industrial sector contributing close to 27% to its GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP Composition by Sector:**

 
 
• The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country is divided into three main sectors: agriculture, industry, and services.
 
• The industrial sector includes manufacturing, mining, construction, and utilities.
 
• The contribution of each sector to the GDP indicates the economic structure and development level of a country.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Sector in Pakistan:**
 
 
• Pakistan's economy is heavily reliant on agriculture, with the services sector also playing a significant role.
 
• The industrial sector includes textiles, chemicals, food processing, and steel, but it faces challenges such as energy shortages and political instability.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Analysis:**
 
 
• China's industrial sector is the largest in the world, driven by manufacturing and export-oriented industries.
 
• India's industrial sector is diverse, with significant contributions from IT, automotive, and pharmaceuticals.
 
• Japan is known for its advanced technology and high-quality manufacturing, particularly in electronics and automobiles.
 
 
 
• **Economic Indicators:**
 
 
• GDP growth rate, industrial output, and employment rates are key indicators of the economic health of a country's industrial sector.
 
• Comparing these indicators across countries can provide insights into their economic strengths and weaknesses.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup was hosted by **India**.
 
• The tournament took place from **January 13 to January 29, 2023**.
 
• The matches were held in two cities: **Bhubaneswar and Rourkela**, both in the state of Odisha.
 
• This was the **fourth time** India hosted the Men's Hockey World Cup, with previous occasions being in 1982, 2010, and 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hockey World Cup**

 
 
• The Men's Hockey World Cup is an international field hockey competition organized by the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**.
 
• The tournament was first held in 1971, and it is contested every four years.
 
• The format of the tournament includes a group stage followed by knockout rounds, including quarter-finals, semi-finals, and the final.
 
• The trophy awarded to the winners was designed by the Pakistani Army and introduced in 1971.
 
 
 
• **Odisha's Role**
 
 
• Odisha has emerged as a major hub for hockey in India, with significant investment in sports infrastructure.
 
• The Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar is a renowned venue for international hockey matches.
 
• Rourkela's Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium, which hosted matches in the 2023 World Cup, is one of the largest hockey stadiums in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Hockey**
 
 
• Hosting the World Cup has provided a boost to the sport's popularity and development in India.
 
• It has led to improved infrastructure and training facilities, benefiting both current and future players.
 
• India's performance in international hockey has seen significant improvement in recent years, partly due to these developments.
 
 
 
• **Recent Winners**
 
 
• The 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup, also hosted by India, was won by Belgium.
 
• Australia and the Netherlands have been dominant teams in recent tournaments, with Australia winning in 2010 and 2014, and the Netherlands reaching the finals multiple times.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement related to government expenditure.

options.text: Revenue expenditure directly contributes to GDP growth.
Revenue expenditure impacts assets liability of the government.
Revenue expenditure does not impact assets liability of the government.
Capital expenditure directly contributes to GDP growth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital expenditure directly contributes to GDP growth.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Capital expenditure (CapEx)** is used by the government for the acquisition of assets, such as infrastructure, buildings, and machinery.
 
• It directly contributes to the growth of the country's **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** by enhancing productive capacity.
 
• CapEx has a multiplier effect on the economy, creating jobs and stimulating demand for goods and services.
 
• Examples include spending on roads, bridges, schools, and hospitals, which can boost economic activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure:**

 
 
• Revenue expenditure includes spending on day-to-day operations, such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments.
 
• It does not result in the creation of assets or directly contribute to GDP growth.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding borrowing).
 
• High levels of fiscal deficit can lead to inflation and higher public debt.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• The multiplier effect refers to the increase in final income arising from any new injection of spending.
 
• Capital expenditure usually has a higher multiplier effect compared to revenue expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Public Debt:**
 
 
• Public debt is the total amount of money that a government owes to creditors.
 
• Sustainable levels of public debt are crucial for economic stability.

questions.question: What are the major branches of Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hinayana and Mahayana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hinayana and Mahayana** are the two major branches of Buddhism.
 
• Hinayana, also known as Theravada Buddhism, is considered the more orthodox and conservative branch.
 
• Mahayana Buddhism is known for its liberal and inclusive approach, emphasizing the role of bodhisattvas.
 
• Both branches share common teachings of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) but differ in their practices and interpretations.
 
• Mahayana Buddhism is predominant in East Asia, while Theravada Buddhism is more common in Southeast Asia and Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hinayana (Theravada Buddhism)**

 
 
• Emphasizes personal enlightenment and the monastic life.
 
• Relies on the Pali Canon as its scripture.
 
• Focuses on the teachings of the historical Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama.
 
• Practiced mainly in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia.
 
 
 
• **Mahayana Buddhism**
 
 
• Emphasizes the enlightenment of all beings and the role of bodhisattvas.
 
• Includes additional scriptures like the Mahayana Sutras.
 
• Prominent in China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and Tibet.
 
• Incorporates a variety of practices, including Zen and Pure Land Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Bodhisattva**
 
 
• An enlightened being who, out of compassion, forgoes nirvana to help others achieve enlightenment.
 
• Central figure in Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• Famous bodhisattvas include Avalokiteshvara and Manjushri.
 
 
 
• **Pali Canon**
 
 
• The primary scripture of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• Contains the earliest teachings of the Buddha.
 
• Divided into three sections: Vinaya Pitaka (monastic rules), Sutta Pitaka (discourses), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical texts).

questions.question: A disturbance from the equilibrium exchange rate gives rise to automatic forces that push the exchange rate back towards the equilibrium level is known as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stable foreign exchange market**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A stable foreign exchange market is characterized by automatic adjustments that move the exchange rate back towards equilibrium after a disturbance.
 
• These adjustments are driven by market forces such as supply and demand for foreign currency.
 
• A stable market ensures that any short-term volatility in the exchange rate is corrected over time.
 
• This stability is crucial for international trade and investment, as it reduces uncertainty for businesses and investors.
 
• Central banks may intervene occasionally to maintain stability but rely primarily on market mechanisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equilibrium Exchange Rate:**

 
 
• The equilibrium exchange rate is the rate at which the supply of a currency equals the demand for that currency.
 
• It is determined by various factors including inflation rates, interest rates, and economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Exchange Rates:**
 
 
• Interest rates: Higher interest rates offer lenders a better return relative to other countries.
 
• Economic performance: Strong economic performance attracts foreign investment, increasing demand for the currency.
 
 
 
• **Intervention by Central Banks:**
 
 
• Central banks may buy or sell their own currency to influence the exchange rate.
 
• Such interventions are usually aimed at stabilizing or correcting misalignments in the exchange rate.
 
 
 
• **Exchange Rate Regimes:**
 
 
• Floating exchange rate: The value of the currency is determined by the market forces of supply and demand.
 
• Fixed exchange rate: The value of the currency is pegged to another major currency like the USD.
